[AIM]: Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) is one of the most significant cardiovascular complications in patients with diabetes. Ubiquitin conjugating enzyme 9 (UBC9) is the only SUMO-E2 enzyme that plays a key role in cardiomyocytes homeostasis. This study aimed to elucidate the roles and mechanisms of UBC9 in DCM development.
[METHODS]: We established cardiomyocyte-specific UBC9 knockout mice and UBC9-overexpressing mice in vivo. A DCM model was established by feeding a high-fat diet and administering a low-dose streptozotocin injection. Proteomics, H&E staining, Sirius Red staining, WGA staining, real-time PCR, and western blotting were performed to examine fibrosis, hypertrophy, and mitophagy in the myocardium. Neonatal mouse cardiomyocytes (NMCMs) were cultured in vitro and stimulated with palmitic acid, UBC9 overexpression adenovirus, and small interfering RNA to establish UBC9 overexpression or knockdown NMCMs. Real-time PCR, western blotting, and immunoprecipitation were employed to examine the roles and mechanisms of UBC9 in cardiomyocyte mitophagy.
[RESULTS]: The transcription and protein levels of UBC9 were significantly decreased in the myocardium of DCM mice. Cardiomyocyte-specific UBC9 knockout aggravated cardiac dysfunction, myocardial fibrosis, hypertrophy, and impaired mitophagy. Conversely, UBC9 overexpression produced opposite effects. UBC9 protected cardiomyocyte mitophagy independently of SUMOylation. UBC9 exerted protective effects against defective cardiomyocyte mitophagy by directly binding to NEDD4, enhancing RUNX2 ubiquitination and degradation, which in turn increased PSEN2 expression. Moreover, the impact of UBC9 on cardiomyocyte mitophagy was reversed upon PSEN2 knockdown.
[CONCLUSIONS]: UBC9 alleviated DCM development through the NEDD4/RUNX2/PSEN2 pathway. These findings offer novel insights into the potential of UBC9 as a therapeutic target for DCM.

key_findings.finding: Direct primary evidence supports a requirement for UBC9/UBE2I in cardiomyocyte protein quality control: in neonatal cardiomyocytes, UBC9 siRNA caused accumulation of aggregated protein and reduced UPS function measured with the GFPu/CL1 degron reporter, whereas UBC9 overexpression enhanced UPS activity. In a cardiomyocyte-specific CryAB(R120G) desmin-related proteotoxicity model, UBC9 overexpression reduced aggregates, while UBC9 knockdown worsened UPS impairment and aggregate accumulation. PMID 25097219.

source_tools.relevance: Primary-paper abstract and results preview directly report cardiomyocyte UBC9 knockdown, GFPu UPS assay, CryAB(R120G) aggregates, and rescue/worsening outcomes.

key_findings.finding: A complementary primary study links UBC9 to autophagic clearance under cardiac proteotoxic stress. In neonatal rat ventricular cardiomyocytes, gain/loss of UBC9 altered autophagic flux; cardiomyocyte UBC9-transgenic mice showed increased baseline autophagy. In the cardiomyocyte-specific CryAB(R120G) model, UBC9 overexpression reduced aggregates, fibrosis, hypertrophy, and improved cardiac function/survival. PMID 27142163.

source_tools.relevance: Primary-paper abstract and results preview directly support UBC9 gain/loss effects on autophagic flux and the in-vivo proteotoxic cardiac model.

key_findings.finding: Newer direct genetic evidence extends the requirement to diabetic cardiomyopathy/mitophagy: cardiomyocyte-specific Ubc9 knockout aggravated cardiac dysfunction, fibrosis, hypertrophy, and impaired mitophagy, while overexpression was protective. The reported mechanism was UBC9 binding to NEDD4, enhancing RUNX2 ubiquitination/degradation and increasing PSEN2; effects were reversed by PSEN2 knockdown. key_findings.finding: The overall interpretation is that UBC9 is required for efficient, but not necessarily absolutely indispensable, cardiomyocyte proteostasis: loss/knockdown produces UPS failure, aggregate accumulation, or impaired autophagic/mitophagic clearance, while increased UBC9 is protective in stress models. The strongest direct evidence concerns siRNA loss-of-function and cardiomyocyte-specific knockout in disease models; the 2014/2016 studies do not establish a complete adult-heart null phenotype or prove that all effects require canonical SUMO conjugation.
